Intended flu vaccination and international collaboration (Liu et al. 2024)

Source: R/data.R
fluvax.Rd

A survey experiment with 1,334 US adults (an opt-in online panel): respondents were asked whether they would take a flu vaccine developed by the United States alone, through a US-China collaboration, or through a US-Japan collaboration, the version randomly assigned (Liu et al. 2024). The answer is no, don't know, or yes; "don't know" may mix respondents undecided between the other answers with respondents who give it whatever the vaccine, a candidate inflated alternative for imnl().

Usage

data(fluvax)

Format

A data frame with 1,334 rows and 9 variables:

vaccinate

Factor: no, dont_know, yes (would take the vaccine this year).

condition

Factor, the randomized origin of the vaccine: us_alone, us_china, us_japan.

party

Factor: democrat, independent, republican (leaners counted with their party), other (another party or unclassified).

age

Age in years (81 = older than 80).

female

1 if female (sex assigned at birth).

educ

Education: 1 (8th grade or less), 2 (some high school), 3 (high school), 4 (some college), 5 (associate's degree), 7 (bachelor's degree), 8 (graduate degree); the survey's codes, used as a score in the published model.

income

Household income in 16 brackets, 1 (less than 10,000 dollars) to 16 (150,000 dollars or more).

race

Factor: white, black (each alone), other (any other or several).

knowledge

Share of four political-knowledge questions answered correctly.

Source

Liu, R., Nagao, H., Hatungimana, W., Zhang, J.J. and Kennedy, J.J. (2024). The politics of flu vaccines: International collaboration and political partisanship. Japanese Journal of Political Science, 25, 61-74. doi:10.1017/S1468109924000021

Provenance and terms

From the replication archive of Liu et al. (2024) at the Harvard Dataverse (doi:10.7910/DVN/BYAFJR , version 1.0, released under CC0 1.0): the file Data.dta (md5 40cad902c1e17f2de59b6dac0aacc5da), the raw survey items, from which every variable is rebuilt as the deposit's DoFile.do builds it for Table 3, Model 1 (the codes are those of the deposit's codebook). The rows are the 1,334 respondents of that model. The rebuilding script is data-raw/make_examples.R of the development repository; with se = "robust" the coefficients and standard errors of Table 3, Model 1 reproduce to the printed three decimals.

See also

Other datasets: afghan_leaders, bes1987, bes2010, cabinets, defection, pa2006, pres2004, sanctions

Examples

data(fluvax)
table(fluvax$vaccinate, fluvax$condition)
#>            
#>             us_alone us_china us_japan
#>   no             130      154      108
#>   dont_know      103      111      101
#>   yes            216      174      237
m <- mnl(vaccinate ~ condition + age + female + educ + income + race + party + knowledge,
         data = fluvax, se = "robust")
summary(m)
#> Multinomial logit 
#> Call: mnl(formula = vaccinate ~ condition + age + female + educ + income + 
#>     race + party + knowledge, data = fluvax, se = "robust")

#> Standard errors: robust. Log-likelihood -1281.466 on 26 parameters, 1334 cases. AIC 2614.93, BIC 2750.03.
first_difference(m, "condition", from = "us_alone", to = "us_china")
#> First differences: condition from us_alone to us_china at the covariate profile (delta intervals at 95%)
#>  alternative  from    to   diff  lower  upper
#>           no 0.186 0.238  0.052  0.001  0.102
#>    dont_know 0.207 0.234  0.027 -0.028  0.083
#>          yes 0.607 0.528 -0.079 -0.151 -0.007
# \donttest{
## "don't know" as a mixture of the undecided and of routine non-answerers
mi <- imnl(vaccinate ~ condition + age + female + educ + income + race + party + knowledge |
             age + educ + knowledge, data = fluvax, inflate = "dont_know")
#> The inflated likelihood has 2 distinct local maxima among the ends of the search from 14 starts (log-likelihoods about -1276.9, -1279.6); the highest is reported. The search also ended at 1 point that is not a maximum (a boundary, a saddle, or no convergence). See object$search.
compare_models(MNL = m, inflated = mi)
#>     model
#>       MNL
#>  inflated
#>                                                                       type
